venue_analysis.downtown_linden_corner: Cafe, $. Lots of meat-free dishes; light and fresh; deskmate with peanut allergy eats the whole menu safely; oat milk by default, olive oil instead of butter, white beans instead of cream. Meets every constraint: 3 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_slate_window: Satay (peanut) dressing on every grain bowl and peanuts roasted in-house. Deal-breaker for Cyrus: 0 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_wren_house: Every dish has meat or fish. Deal-breaker for Mina: 0 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_paper_kite: Peanut-free, vegetarian half, light. But heavy dairy throughout. Misses Roxy's intolerance: 2 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_marble_steps: Vegetarian-friendly, peanut- and dairy-safe (sister example), but heavy fried food. Misses Brooke's wholesome preference: 2 stars.

notes: Cyrus's peanut allergy is only implied by 'no satay incident sequel'; a player must know satay is peanut-based. Fair but the most subtle clue, and it is the only allergy signal in the chat.
Mina's vegetarianism is likewise implied (sushi day, 'zero meat' section) rather than stated. Readable.

Linden Corner's peanut safety is conveyed only indirectly (deskmate with auto-injector never needed it), not by an explicit 'no peanuts'. Same indirect style is used for Marble Steps. Consistent, not unfair.

Each decoy fails exactly one constraint, which makes the elimination clean. Marble Steps vs Linden Corner hinges on Brooke's 'wholesome' line; Paper Kite vs Linden Corner hinges on Roxy's dairy line. Both clearly signposted.
No budget is mentioned in the chat; all venues are $, so price is a non-factor.
